name: JEN Elettronica
dirt_evidence: Vox V828 Tone Bender / JEN Jumbo Fuzz / JEN Harmon Booster / Vox Stereo Fuzz Wah
notes: JEN was established in Italy around 1967 and became a major OEM effects manufacturer, producing effects for Vox and other brands while also marketing pedals under the JEN name. The V828 Tone Bender and later Jumbo Fuzz provide strong dirt-product evidence. Preserve JEN as a physical manufacturer/OEM node, not as a synonym for every brand it serviced.

name: Herald Electronics
notes: Effects Database documents the Herald Electronics AM-44A Fuzz Master as a Japanese-made late-1960s/1970s fuzz distributed under multiple regional brand names including Apollo, LRE, Melos, Mica, Monacor and Olson. This is a strong manufacturer-level discovery because the product is tied to a period Herald catalog and a distinct OEM-style multi-brand trail.

name: Selmer
notes: Selmer documented and advertised a Fuzz-Wah by 1968. Selmer engineer John Weir's surviving account states management asked him to design the pedal in 1968, and period advertising in Melody Maker confirms a Selmer Fuzz-Wah product. A later version appears to have been sourced from the Far East, so manufacturing identity should remain split by production period.

name: Cav. Giovanni Moreschi / Moreschi
notes: Moreschi, a Castelfidardo maker better known for accordions, produced a short-lived effects line in cooperation with Gary Hurst / Electronic Sounds. The Moreschi Octave Fuzz and Wah-Fuzz provide concrete dirt-product evidence and show another unusual European manufacturing node outside the standard British/U.S. circuit-family pathways.
